hints: Focus on what acid rain actually is, dissolved acids like sulfuric and nitric acid falling in rain, and what acids can attack down at ground level.
Think about what acids do to carbonate stone, to reactive metals, and to ions in soil, all three are classic acid reactions.
Now ask yourself which process happens high up in the stratosphere with a completely different set of chemicals, and that will be the odd one out.
walkthrough:
**Recall what acid rain contains**

Think of acid rain as dilute sulfuric acid and nitric acid in rainwater, with pH often below 5.6.

These come mainly from $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{NO}_x$ from burning fossil fuels:
$$\text{SO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_3 \text{ then oxidised to } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$$

**Check the true ground-level effects**

Acids react with limestone and marble buildings, with metals like iron, and they wash ions out of soil. That makes erosion of stone, corrosion of metals, and leaching of nutrients all real effects of acid rain.

**Spot the unrelated environmental issue**

Ozone depletion is destruction of $\text{O}_3$ in the stratosphere, mainly by CFCs and related radicals, not by $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ or $\text{HNO}_3$ in rain. So the ozone statement does not describe acid rain.

options.A: This is a true effect of acid rain, so it is not the answer. Acid attacks calcium carbonate in limestone and marble, for example $\text{CaCO}_3 + 2\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{Ca}^{2+} + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$, causing erosion of stonework.
options.B: This is correct because it does NOT describe acid rain. Ozone depletion is caused by CFCs and other ozone-depleting substances breaking down $\text{O}_3$ in the stratosphere, a completely separate issue from acidic precipitation.
options.C: This is a true effect of acid rain, so it is not the answer. Extra $\text{H}^+$ ions speed up oxidation and acid attack on metals such as iron and steel, increasing corrosion.
options.D: This is a true effect of acid rain, so it is not the answer. $\text{H}^+$ ions displace essential cations like $\text{Ca}^{2+}$, $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ and $\text{K}^+$ from soil and also mobilise toxic $\text{Al}^{3+}$, damaging plants and aquatic life.
